question: A commercial driver license is required to drive a bus designed to seat how many persons, including the driver?
explanation: The manual states bus drivers must have a CDL if they drive a vehicle designed to seat 16 or more persons, including the driver.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: To earn a passenger endorsement, you must pass a knowledge test covering which sections of the manual?
choice_c: Sections 2 and 4 (plus Section 5 if your bus has air brakes)
explanation: The manual states you must pass a knowledge test on Sections 2 and 4 to get the passenger endorsement, and also on Section 5 if your bus has air brakes.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

topic: Signing the previous driver's inspection report
question: Before driving, when may you sign a previous driver's vehicle inspection report certifying its defects are addressed?
choice_a: Only if defects reported earlier have been certified as repaired or not needing repair
choice_c: Only if you personally repaired the defects yourself
choice_d: Never; each driver must file a separate report
explanation: The manual states you should sign the previous driver's report only if defects reported earlier have been certified as repaired or as not needing repair.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: Per the manual's vehicle inspection list, what tire restriction applies specifically to a bus's front wheels?
choice_a: They must be studded tires in winter
choice_b: They must match the rear tires' brand
choice_c: They must be inflated to maximum rated pressure
choice_d: They must not have recapped or re-grooved tires
explanation: Among the vehicle systems to check, the manual specifies that front wheels must not have recapped or re-grooved tires.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: The manual requires a bus to carry which of the following emergency reflective equipment?
choice_b: 3 reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares
explanation: The manual requires the bus to have the fire extinguisher and emergency reflectors: 3 reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

topic: Never drive with an open emergency exit
question: According to the manual, what must never happen while driving a bus?
choice_b: Locking a roof hatch in a partly open position
choice_c: Turning on the red emergency door light at night
choice_d: Driving with an open emergency exit door or window
explanation: The manual states you should never drive with an open emergency exit door or window.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: What is the "standee line" described in the manual?
choice_a: A line marking where luggage must be stored
choice_b: A line indicating the bus's maximum speed
choice_c: A line on the floor, behind which standing riders must remain, with no rider standing forward of the rear of the driver's seat
choice_d: A boarding queue line painted outside the bus
explanation: The manual states no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat, and buses that allow standing must have a line (the standee line) showing riders where they cannot stand; all standing riders must stay behind it.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Per the manual, buses must never carry:
choice_a: Explosives in the space occupied by people, except small-arms ammunition
explanation: The manual lists explosives in the space occupied by people (except small-arms ammunition) as something buses must never carry, while small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs are explicitly allowed.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

topic: Hazardous material weight limits on buses
question: Per the manual, buses must never carry more than:
choice_a: 1,000 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials
choice_b: 250 pounds of any one hazard class
choice_d: 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class
explanation: The manual states buses must never carry more than 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Why does the manual advise charter bus drivers not to allow riders on the bus until departure time?
choice_c: To help prevent theft or vandalism of the bus
choice_d: To allow more time for the after-trip inspection
explanation: The manual states charter bus drivers should not allow riders on the bus until departure time, which will help prevent theft or vandalism of the bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: According to the manual, what does it mean if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve?
choice_b: The road is properly banked for your speed
choice_c: The bus's suspension needs immediate repair
explanation: The manual states that if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, you are driving too fast.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: Per the manual, you should stop your bus how far before a railroad crossing?
explanation: The manual states to stop your bus between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: If your bus has a manual transmission, what does the manual say you should never do while crossing railroad tracks?
explanation: The manual states that if your bus has a manual transmission, you should never change gears while crossing the tracks.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: The manual says to stop at least how many feet before the draw of a drawbridge that has no signal light or traffic control attendant?
explanation: The manual states to stop at drawbridges that do not have a signal light or traffic control attendant, at least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: If you work for an interstate carrier, what must you do at the end of each shift, per the manual?
choice_a: Complete a written inspection report for each bus driven, listing any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown
choice_b: File a report only if damage occurred
choice_c: Report defects verbally to the next driver only
explanation: The manual states interstate carrier drivers must complete a written inspection report for each bus driven at the end of each shift, specifying the bus and listing any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown (or stating there are none).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

topic: Prohibited practices: fueling with riders aboard
question: Per the manual's prohibited practices, when should you avoid fueling a bus with riders on board?
choice_b: Unless absolutely necessary, and never in a closed building with riders aboard
choice_c: Only if the bus has more than 30 seats
choice_d: There is no restriction on fueling with riders aboard
explanation: The manual states to avoid fueling your bus with riders on board unless absolutely necessary, and to never refuel in a closed building with riders on board.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

topic: Towing or pushing a disabled bus
question: According to the manual's prohibited practices, when is it acceptable to tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard?
choice_b: Only on highways with a speed limit under 45 mph
choice_c: Whenever the employer's insurance allows it
choice_d: Only when getting off would be unsafe, and only to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers
explanation: The manual states not to tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard unless getting off would be unsafe, and to only tow or push the bus to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: What does the brake-door interlock system on urban mass transit coaches do, per the manual?
choice_a: It automatically opens the rear door when the bus parks
choice_b: It applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, releasing when the door is closed
choice_c: It shuts off the engine if the bus is overloaded
choice_d: It locks the steering wheel whenever the bus is parked
explanation: The manual states the brake and accelerator interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, and releases when you close the rear door.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4

topic: Brake-door interlock is not a parking brake substitute
question: Per the manual, the brake-door interlock safety feature should:
choice_a: Be used in place of the parking brake
choice_c: Only be relied on by charter bus drivers
choice_d: Not be used in place of the parking brake
explanation: The manual explicitly warns not to use the brake-door interlock safety feature in place of the parking brake.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4
